title: Dispatch GID 6: An Audience Appears in the Darkened Lyceum
summary: The covered instrument remains still, but people are heard taking seats.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Police posted outside the sealed Lyceum heard footsteps and the scrape of chairs after midnight. No one had entered the building. Inspector Voss and Dr. Saye found the auditorium empty, yet the two unsold seats were warm. A third chair had been turned toward the covered silvered plate.

Miss Marsh believes the plate opened a line of sight in both directions. Spectators saw different scenes because each was shown a separate view into the Stratum. The voice was common, she says, because the missing attendant reached the place where those views meet. She cannot explain why the auditorium continues to change with the lamp dark.

Halden has admitted that the plate was cut from a mirror recovered during an expedition, not made in his workshop as his programme stated. He says he concealed its origin because he feared the audience would mistake a scientific demonstration for a séance. He still believes the machine has revealed a real place and that Miss Crain can be brought back through it.

Dr. Saye proposes moving the plate off the stage before any further trial. Miss Marsh objects. If the rear aisle opens only when it faces an audience, moving it may close the one route Miss Crain knows. The two have agreed to plan a brief operation with the exits staffed and the plate mounted so it can be turned away at once.

Ruth Crain has asked to attend. “If Mabel can see a roomful of people,” she said, “I want one of them to be looking for her.” Inspector Voss has not yet decided whether to admit anyone beyond the operators.
